chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

That Asma bint Umays had the post-natal bleeding (nifas) of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered her, when she wanted to assume Ihram from Dhi al-Hulayfa, to stuff herself with cotton and rags and enter into Ihram for Hajj.

key_terms.الِاحْرَامَ: the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَحْتَشِيَ: to stuff or pack (with material to stop bleeding)
key_terms.ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhi al-Hulayfa, the designated Miqat (station) for entering Ihram

ai.seo_question: How did Asma bint Umays perform Ihram for Hajj while in post-natal bleeding?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual purity, where Asma bint Umays was permitted to use cotton and rags as a barrier to manage post-natal bleeding (nifas) rather than requiring a full ritual bath. It underscores the principle that major ritual states like Ihram can be assumed even with minor impurities if a physical barrier is used, reflecting the Prophet's emphasis on ease for women in specific biological conditions. This incident is frequently cited by scholars to justify the use of 'istihada' (irregular bleeding) rulings for women who cannot perform ghusl immediately before Hajj.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/296] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara from Abi Ja’far عليه السلام

who said: Asma bt. Umays had the Nifas [post-natal bleeding] of Muhammad b. Abi Bakr [after delivering him] and wanted to assume Ihram at Dhi al-Hulayfa so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ordered her to stuff pieces of cotton and rags [to stop the blood flow] and enter into Ihram [proclaim Talbiyya] for Hajj ...
